title: Choose the visual world for brickbot.ro
question: The roll assigned The Annual. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Annual
options.lineage: club annuals and yearbooks, bound in black, signed by everyone in them
options.thesis: Each season is a volume of BrickBot's annual, signed in yellow by the people it changed.
options.viewport: Volume XI opens: the season's big team photo set like the annual's first spread, a plain set headline, marker notes scrawled across the photo by members; 'Partner with us' is the patrons' page tab, always visible.
options.risk: A yearbook is a school object. Set timidly it reads as a school project, which you asked to avoid; it only works as a premium club annual.

raised.raise: Volumes I–XI (2016–2026) run as a strict numbered index in a margin column on every page.
Every result, award and figure sits on one measured grid in tabular figures, so the energy reads as performance.
Exactly one yellow thing is lit per spread; the yellow is rationed, never sprayed.
Total material commitment: the whole page is one bound object, not sections on a dark template.
Every volume is dated and placed (venue, city), like the annual's colophon.

options.label: The Kit
options.lineage: sports-club identity: match shirts, squad numbers, sponsor patches
options.thesis: BrickBot as a club: the yellow shirt, the number 15996, and sponsors' logos on the kit.
options.viewport: 15996 set enormous like a shirt back, cropped by the screen; the team photo inside the numerals; one line on who BrickBot is; 'Put your logo on our shirt' as the main action.
options.risk: Familiar: sports-club sites look like this, and done loosely it drifts toward esports branding.

options.label: The Season Issue
options.thesis: Each season published as an issue: a strict two-column grid, full-bleed photos, the bolt hidden once on every page.
options.viewport: Issue XI cover: the BrickBot masthead over a full-bleed Worlds photo with the bolt hidden in it; cover lines link to the season, partnering and joining.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: seasons map to issues, as they do in the CMS. Loses on recognition: sponsors and teenagers don't read 1960s magazines.
options.risk: Can turn into an editorial costume; serif plus hairline rules is a look many sites already ship.

options.label: Signal Bench
options.lineage: CRT oscilloscope on a signal bench
options.thesis: The team's energy as a live trace on an etched graticule.
options.viewport: A yellow trace sweeping a graticule, readouts for seasons and awards.
options.case: Declined: an instrument costume that drifts toward the neon look you ruled out, and sponsors don't recognise themselves in it.

options.label: Fold Sequence
options.thesis: Brick by brick as a numbered build sequence.
options.viewport: One sheet folding toward the robot step by step.
options.case: Declined: a teaching diagram, weak on energy and on the people.

options.label: Neon Night
options.thesis: Stacked neon signage on rain-black towers.
options.viewport: A tower of glowing signs with one red accent.
options.case: Declined: exactly the gamer/neon cliché you ruled out, and it forces colours off the brand.

options.label: Floated Pigment
options.thesis: Pigment combed across a bath, lifted once.
options.viewport: A marbled yellow-and-burgundy field you comb with the pointer.
options.case: Declined: beautiful, but says nothing about robots, results or people.
options.risk: Art piece, not a team site.

options.label: Sleeping City
options.thesis: Streets fold into blankets under one night.
options.viewport: Focșani folding into a quilt at night.
options.case: Declined: dreamy and soft, the opposite of electric.
options.kept: Every view anchored to a real place.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark robotics-team site with a yellow accent, executed with full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Team photo hero with a headline and two buttons, then numbers, season, posts and sponsors.
canonCard.risk: Close to the removed first attempt; it reads like every other team's site.
